explanation: A [[kw:compound event]] is the union (or) or intersection (and) of two events.
The union of A and B, written $A \text{ or } B$, includes all outcomes in A, in B, or in both.
The intersection of A and B, written $A \text{ and } B$, includes only outcomes that are in both A and B.
Two events are [[kw:disjoint]] (or [[kw:mutually exclusive]]) if they have no outcomes in common. Their Venn diagram circles do not overlap.
Two events are [[kw:overlapping]] if they share at least one outcome. Their Venn diagram circles intersect.

notes: If A and B overlap, this formula counts the intersection twice.
formulaCard.title: Addition Rule for Disjoint Events

explanation: If events A and B are [[imp:disjoint]] (no overlap), the probability that either occurs is the sum of their probabilities.
Formula: $$ P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) $$
This works because the events share no outcomes, so there's no double-counting.
Example: Drawing a 10 or a face card from a deck — disjoint, so P(10 or face) = 4/52 + 12/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.

discoveryHook.scenario: If you want to find the chance of drawing a 10 or a face card from a deck, you can just add the individual probabilities because no card is both a 10 and a face card. For disjoint events, 'or' means simple addition!

confusionCorner.body: The most common mistake is adding P(A) + P(B) and stopping. If the events overlap, you've counted the intersection twice. [[imp:Always check if there's overlap before using the addition rule.]]
confusionCorner.title: Don't Forget to Subtract!

explanation: For overlapping events, you must avoid double-counting the intersection.
The General Addition Rule: $$ P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B) $$
This formula works for all events, disjoint or overlapping. If disjoint, $ P(A \text{ and } B) = 0 $, and it becomes the simple addition rule.
To use it, identify the intersection outcomes and find their probability.
Example: Face card or spade — P(face) = 12/52, P(spade) = 13/52, P(face and spade) = 3/52, so P = 12/52 + 13/52 − 3/52 = 22/52 = 11/26.

notes: If disjoint, $P(A \text{ and } B)=0$, so it reduces to simple addition.

formulaCard.title: Law of Total Probability (Two Cases)
formulaCard.formula: $$ P(B) = P(A) \cdot P(B \mid A) + P(\overline{A}) \cdot P(B \mid \overline{A}) $$

explanation: Real-life problems often combine [[imp:multiple probability rules]].
A [[kw:probability tree diagram]] helps organize sequences of dependent or independent events.
To find the total probability of an event that can occur in several ways, use: $$ P(B) = P(A \text{ and } B) + P(\overline{A} \text{ and } B) $$ This is the [[kw:Law of Total Probability]].
Multiply along branches for 'and', then add the branch probabilities for 'or'.
Example: A test for a disease: P(correct) = P(has disease and correct) + P(no disease and correct).

discoveryHook.scenario: Whenever you see 'or' in a probability question, pause! Are the events disjoint or overlapping? Using the Probability Blueprint will guide you to the right formula every time.

rows.1: List outcomes of A and B. Find if any outcome belongs to both.
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

explanation: Blueprint for compound 'or' probability:
1. [[imp:Understand]]: Define events A and B. Are they disjoint (no overlap) or overlapping? Use a Venn diagram or list outcomes.
2. [[imp:Solve]]: If disjoint, use $ P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) $. If overlapping, use $ P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B) $.
3. [[imp:Conclude]]: Calculate and interpret the probability. Check if it makes sense (should be between 0 and 1).
For multi-step problems, draw a tree diagram, multiply for paths, then add the paths for 'or'.

confusionCorner.title: Don't Assume Disjoint
confusionCorner.body: Always check for overlap before deciding which formula to use. If you aren't sure, the general addition rule (with subtraction) is always safe – if there's no overlap, P(A and B)=0 and it still works.
